subject.title: fix(sqlite): allow verified shared wal backports

question: Should OpenClaw permit a deployment-set value to waive the SQLite WAL-reset corruption guard for shared system libraries, and if so what auditable evidence or supported verification mechanism is required?
rationale: This is a permanent data-safety and operator-support contract, not a mechanical test or wording choice; source inspection cannot establish which distribution backports OpenClaw should trust or how that trust must be verified.

options.title: Retain fail-closed protection
options.body: Reject unsafe reported versions until the system library presents a version line already covered by the current safety contract.

options.title: Design audited backport support
options.body: Define a maintainable distro/package verification or Doctor-owned workflow, then revise the PR to use that explicit contract.

options.title: Accept a documented operator waiver
options.body: Allow the environment override as a knowingly unsupported risk waiver and document that OpenClaw cannot validate the installed backport.

recommendation.title: Retain fail-closed protection
recommendation.body: Reject unsafe reported versions until the system library presents a version line already covered by the current safety contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work most recently maintained the same SQLite safety diagnostic and adjacent tests, so they are a relevant technical routing contact for the safety-contract decision.
